Cal Rivera: Quick question — I was on a customer trip in Chile during the year-end shutdown and couldn't take my floating holiday. It never got submitted (no reliable wifi). Can that floating day be carried over or converted? Payroll says cutoffs are strict.
Marisol (People Ops): Sorry that happened, Cal. We do allow exceptions for customer travel but need manager sign-off + travel dates. Which date was the day you missed? Also which regional payroll (LATAM) did payroll mention?
Cal Rivera: The day was Dec 28. I was offsite the whole day for demos. Payroll flagged LATAM region cutoff and said unused floats auto-expire unless an exception is logged before 12/31. I didn't know about the auto-submit.
Jenny H.: Yep I can confirm Cal was on a customer site that day — I approved travel but missed the float request. @Marisol (People Ops) I can add a quick note approving carryover. What form do you need?
Marisol (People Ops): Thanks Jenny. Please reply in this thread with a one-line approval (manager approval + reason + dates) and attach any travel confirmation to the HR mailbox. We will escalate to payroll for a manual adjustment if submitted by next Friday (payroll cutoff exception window).
Cal Rivera: Thanks — I pasted a screenshot of the travel confirmation to the HR mailbox just now. Jenny — can you post the one-liner here so it's all in thread?
Jenny H.: Approve: Jenny H., manager of Cal Rivera — approved carryover of floating holiday Dec 28 due to mandatory on-site customer work.
Marisol (People Ops): Perfect. Payroll Bot — can you confirm LATAM manual adjustment window and whether we need a ticket?
Payroll Bot: payroll-bot: Received request. LATAM manual adjustment requires manager approval + HR request ticket. Cutoff exception window open until 2024-01-05 23:59 UTC for this batch. Please file ticket at payroll.redwood/cases with subject "Floating carryover exception - Cal Rivera".
Cal Rivera: Filing ticket now. Quick follow-up — does this affect accrual for next year? I don't want to lose accruals or bonus eligibility because of this admin thing.
Marisol (People Ops): Good Q. One carried-over floating day does not affect accrual rates. If there was unpaid LOA or extended unpaid time that changed FTE, that can impact accrual proration. Since you were full-time and only traveled, accruals remain the same. Payroll will confirm once they process.
Cal Rivera: Awesome — thanks everyone. Appreciate the fast help. :raised_hands:
Marisol (People Ops): No problem — ping me if payroll needs more docs. If ticket is accepted we'll confirm when the carryover posts.
